comment.narrative: No dialogue platforms on public sector reforms within key public sector institutions
1.1 Public Service Sexual Harassment Policy Developed. 1.2 Baseline study on citizen satisfaction/perceptions towards public service delivery in Zimbabwe conducted.

1.1 A baseline survey on sexual harassment in the public service was conducted as part of promoting evidence-based decision-making and enhance citizen participation in government policies, programmes and projects. The data gathered was used to strengthen the draft Public Service Sexual Harassment Policy that was developed by the PSC and to develop training and educational materials on Sexual and Gender Based Violence including prevention and response mechanisms for public service employees under the Public Service Academy. A Sexual Harassment Policy is now in place and work on the development of a Gender and Sexual Harassment Module is in progress. The Sexual Harassment Policy was adopted by the Government of Zimbabwe in Cabinet meeting in April 2022.
1.2 Baseline study on citizen satisfaction/perceptions towards public service delivery in Zimbabwe was conducted. Validations conducted with line ministries, tripartite partners (OPC-MOFED-PSC). Survey part of the key indicators under the National Development Strategy (NDS1) Governance thematic area. Recommendations from the study are set to establish performance indicators for a new work Culture Blueprint and its institutionalization.

1.1 A scoping study on existing Public Service Academy Training Institutes’ ICT infrastructure conducted 1.2 Procurement of ICT equipment for phased implementation of the E-LMS Public Service Academy 1.3 Baseline survey to inform disability inclusion in government policies and national programmes conducted.

1.1 UNDP supported the first phase of the establishment of an E-Learning Management System (E-LMS) for 13 public service training institutes. A Joint ICT scoping Assessment was conducted in partnership with the PSC, the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services and Office of the President and Cabinet.The study found a need to replace obsolete and malfunctioning hardware (desktops, laptops, and printers) at all PSTIs with higher specification gadgets at the training institutions; need to ensure full licensing of all software being used in the PSTIs, including dedicated licensed/proprietary packages for online engagements, need to upgrade all Institutional Local Area Networks (LAN) to fast-speed internet which can effectively run e-LMS. Procurement of 22 laptops and 2 servers for the E-LMS initiated.
1.2 The baseline survey, which is currently ongoing, is intended to obtain reliable and relevant data on disability inclusion within the public service. The information obtained from the study will be used to inform programmatic interventions focused on Persons with Disabilities, especially their inclusion in public policy issues and national development processes and protection of human rights. This will enhance capacities of Government institutions including the PSC to develop policies and programmes that are sensitive to the rights of persons with disabilities

1.1.1 Comprehensive paper on strategic roles of OPC,PSC and MOFED in driving government wide PSR reforms 1.2.1 Development of a structured, comprehensive roadmap on PSR for implementation, with clear prioritisation and sequancing of initiatives and costed results

High Level PSR policy meetings held to validate the PSR strategy. 5 virtual consultative meetings were held through key informant interviews (Government, independent commissions, CSOs, development partners, private sector and Private sector unions) as part of the validation of the draft PSR strategy. The stakeholders noted that the PSR strategy is an important document that covers all the important areas for the transformation of the public sector. However, the stakeholders noted that the success of the strategy goes beyond the articulation of the goals and strategic objectives to making sure that it is implemented and monitored.
